scope: Shared original IP socket OFDs for IPv4/IPv6 sendto/recvfrom/sendmsg/recvmsg/sendmmsg, common owner/worker message ABI, accepted input/output and batch state, existing event waits and original SIGPIPE handoff.
method: Four independent processes, 1,000 iterations each, four Trames vCPUs, three unprofiled counterbalanced before/after repeats plus a separate diagnostic repeat. Single-message iterations send and receive a checked 64-byte two-vector payload. Batch iterations invoke SYS_sendmmsg directly for eight 64-byte messages and verify each recvmsg; stream receives complete each checked frame across any short reads. Endpoint setup/cleanup is outside the loop timer. Native ARM Linux executes the identical static musl ELF on six vCPUs; it is stopped before Mac timing. Native macOS has its own ABI and uses eight POSIX sendmsg calls for the batch reference. Different kernels/APIs/CPU counts make native timings contextual. All compilation/affected CI/FFI acceptance finish before final timing. The initial short TCP-poll control median increases; a pre-declared existing control is then checked with 10,000 iterations and nine unprofiled counterbalanced samples. Both data sets are retained; the longer comparison is near equal. No whole-app, Firefox, physical-iPad or generally native-speed claim.

measurement_correction.observation: The stage24 exact recorded ELF and initial stage26 ELF contain a libc sendmmsg wrapper that loops over sendmsg with no sendmmsg SVC. Earlier eight-message loop measurements remain those workloads, not kernel sendmmsg throughput. Functional ARM64 SVC-269 tests are unaffected. This stage changes both Linux batch fixture branches to explicit syscall(SYS_sendmmsg); disassembly verifies number269 passed into syscall, moved to x8, then SVC0. Final loop and native comparisons all use that same corrected ELF. Initial wrapper measurements are retained separately, not mixed into final rows.

positive partial EAGAIN/EFAULT/EPIPE and short sends

validation.reuse: The final SIGPIPE fixture accepts the connection before shutting down the sender; closing an unaccepted Linux listener caused ECONNRESET rather than the intended EPIPE. Only this changed cfg(test) case and strict checks rerun. Apple full276 and Linux other275 results, unchanged production builds/FFI/VFS/network/CPU/memory/graphics acceptance are reused. No production source changed after the measured build.
validation.environment: Initial unprivileged network test launch was denied local socket permissions; affected tests reran with loopback access. iOS build uses the full Xcode DEVELOPER_DIR rather than system-default CommandLineTools. No source workaround or new guest permission policy.

implementation.ownership: Original full shared SocketOperation, not numeric FD re-resolution or copied resource counters.
implementation.abi: Same prepared decoder for owner and worker IP messages; original Socket transport/policy/accounting. Captured send inputs and receive outputs survive waits.
implementation.synchronization: Per-accepted-call progress mutex and relaxed signal flag only. Existing socket publication guard applies separately per message, not across the batch. No global resource lock, service thread, bus, busy polling or ordinary guest-memory fence.
implementation.waits: Existing native/hybrid/packet-stack event sources and deadlines, subscribe before retry, return execution slot, recheck only parked receive destinations before dequeue.
implementation.signals: Save terminal result and partial batch count, hand original task effects to owner, never resend to rediscover EPIPE. One accepted seccomp entry.
